controls.statement: The problem, intended users, release scope, non-goals, and deferred features are documented.
controls.primary_reason: The five product-definition elements are explicit document fields whose presence and version binding can be checked mechanically.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The product definition contains problem, intended users, release scope, non-goals, and deferred-feature sections.

controls.statement: Critical journeys cover onboarding, normal use, error recovery, account recovery, cancellation, and data/account deletion where applicable.
controls.primary_reason: A declared capability matrix makes applicability finite, allowing exact coverage checks for the six named critical-journey classes.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The critical-journey register contains onboarding, normal-use, error-recovery, account-recovery, cancellation, and deletion journeys or explicit inapplicability records.

controls.statement: Behavior is specified for unavailable dependencies, partial failures, empty data, malformed data, incomplete data, stale data, and conflicting data.
controls.primary_reason: The seven dependency and data conditions are a finite specification checklist whose behavior references can be validated.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The product specification defines behavior for unavailable dependencies, partial failures, empty, malformed, incomplete, stale, and conflicting data.

controls.statement: Define measurable launch success, failure, stop, and rollback criteria.
controls.primary_reason: Measurable launch criteria are fixed structured predicates, so success, failure, stop, and rollback fields can be checked before launch.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The launch plan defines metric, operator, threshold, window, and action for success, failure, stop, and rollback criteria.

controls.statement: Define who may pause, continue, expand, or roll back the launch.
controls.primary_reason: Launch actions and authorized identities form a finite authority matrix with exact membership checks.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The launch plan assigns authorized roles for pause, continue, expand, and rollback actions.

controls.statement: Establish whether launch is internal, private, regional, percentage-based, invitation-only, or public.
controls.primary_reason: Launch mode is a closed set and can be required as one exact value with any regional or percentage parameters.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The launch plan declares internal, private, regional, percentage-based, invitation-only, or public mode and its required parameters.

controls.statement: Ensure product, marketing, sales, support, and operations use the same release date and scope.
controls.primary_reason: Versioned organization release records can be compared for exact date and scope agreement across the five named functions.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Product, marketing, sales, support, and operations records reference one canonical release identifier.
All five records match the canonical release date and scope digest.

controls.statement: Define the intended outcome and observable evidence that the problem is reduced.
controls.primary_reason: Intended outcome and observable evidence are explicit strategy fields whose metric bindings can be checked.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The strategy defines an intended outcome plus observable measure, data source, window, and change criterion showing problem reduction.

controls.statement: Define strategic non-goals and choices to prevent unbounded scope.
controls.primary_reason: Strategic non-goals and scope-limiting choices are explicit versioned record fields.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The strategy contains non-goals and explicit scope choices with owners and effective dates.

controls.statement: Describe the value exchange, including what users provide in money, data, attention, effort, or lock-in.
controls.primary_reason: The named forms of user contribution are explicit value-exchange fields with declared applicability.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The product strategy describes money, data, attention, effort, and lock-in contributions or records explicit inapplicability for each.

controls.statement: Specify assumptions about demand, willingness, behavior, channels, support, and unit economics.
controls.primary_reason: The seven assumption classes are explicit strategy-record fields with measurable values or hypotheses.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The strategy records assumptions for demand, willingness, behavior, channels, support, and unit economics with identifiers and expected values.

controls.statement: Use multiple evidence sources rather than relying on stakeholder opinion or a single research method.
controls.primary_reason: Evidence-source and method identifiers allow an exact minimum-diversity check that excludes a single stakeholder opinion or method.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each discovery conclusion cites at least two independent evidence sources using at least two research methods.

controls.statement: Separate observed behavior from stated preference and researcher interpretation.
controls.primary_reason: Observed behavior, stated preference, and researcher interpretation are three explicit provenance labels that can be required on research findings.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every research finding labels content separately as observed behavior, stated preference, and researcher interpretation.

controls.statement: Document research questions, sampling, methods, consent, limitations, and analysis approach.
controls.primary_reason: The research-plan elements are an exact finite set of required record fields.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every research record contains questions, sampling plan, methods, consent, limitations, and analysis approach.

controls.statement: Triangulate qualitative findings with behavioral, operational, market, and support evidence.
controls.primary_reason: Triangulation can be represented as a required multi-source evidence graph with the five named evidence classes.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each material qualitative finding links to behavioral, operational, market, and support evidence or explicit inapplicability rationales.

controls.statement: Translate validated findings into traceable requirements, design constraints, and measurable outcomes.
controls.primary_reason: Validated finding identifiers and traceability links make translation into requirements, constraints, and measurable outcomes mechanically checkable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every validated finding links to a requirement or design constraint and to a measurable outcome definition.

controls.statement: Distinguish needs, goals, constraints, functional requirements, quality requirements, interface requirements, and design decisions.
controls.primary_reason: Requirement artifacts can use an exact type enumeration, making category distinction mechanically decidable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every requirements record is labeled need, goal, constraint, functional requirement, quality requirement, interface requirement, or design decision.

controls.statement: State the subject, required behavior or property, conditions, thresholds, units, and tolerances.
controls.primary_reason: The seven requirement elements are explicit typed fields whose presence and units or tolerance relationships can be validated.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every requirement states subject, required behavior or property, conditions, thresholds, units, and tolerances.

controls.statement: Define normal, alternate, exception, degraded, recovery, and prohibited behavior.
controls.primary_reason: The six behavior categories form an exact specification checklist with applicability decisions.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each feature specification defines normal, alternate, exception, degraded, recovery, and prohibited behavior or an explicit inapplicability rationale.

controls.statement: Specify data, state, timing, ordering, concurrency, retention, and authorization semantics.
controls.primary_reason: The named semantic dimensions are explicit requirement fields and can be checked for presence and type.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each applicable requirement specifies data, state, timing, ordering, concurrency, retention, and authorization semantics.

controls.statement: Link every approved requirement to acceptance criteria and planned verification.
controls.primary_reason: Approved requirement identifiers can be joined exactly to acceptance-criteria and planned-verification records.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every approved requirement links to at least one acceptance criterion and one planned verification method.

controls.statement: Preserve history and effective dates; do not silently rewrite accepted requirements.
controls.primary_reason: Append-only versions, effective dates, and immutable accepted revisions can prove history preservation and detect silent rewrites.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every accepted requirement revision remains retrievable by digest with its effective date and successor links.

controls.statement: Identify derived requirements and the assumptions from which they follow.
controls.primary_reason: Derived-requirement labels and assumption provenance are exact traceability relationships.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every derived requirement links to the assumptions and source requirements from which it follows.

controls.statement: Use explicit criteria such as user impact, strategic fit, risk reduction, urgency, learning value, cost, reversibility, and dependency value.
controls.primary_reason: An explicit prioritization model can be required to name and score the stated decision criteria with versioned definitions.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The prioritization record defines user impact, strategic fit, risk reduction, urgency, learning value, cost, reversibility, and dependency value criteria.

controls.statement: Include reliability, security, privacy, accessibility, maintenance, support, and debt work in the same prioritization system.
controls.primary_reason: The prioritization registry can be checked for entries from every named non-feature work category.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Reliability, security, privacy, accessibility, maintenance, support, and debt work use the same prioritization registry as feature work.

controls.statement: Make stakeholder influence and mandatory obligations visible rather than hiding them inside scores.
controls.primary_reason: Separate influence and obligation fields make hidden inclusion inside aggregate scores mechanically detectable.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every priority item records stakeholder influence and mandatory obligations outside its aggregate score.

controls.statement: Represent uncertainty and sensitivity instead of treating prioritization scores as objective truth.
controls.primary_reason: Uncertainty, sensitivity, and interpretation warnings are explicit prioritization-record fields.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each prioritization result records uncertainty, sensitivity analysis, and a statement that the score is decision support rather than objective truth.

controls.statement: Identify prerequisites, sequencing constraints, migration needs, and operational readiness work.
controls.primary_reason: Prerequisites, sequencing, migrations, and operational-readiness work are explicit dependency-graph node and edge types.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every roadmap item records applicable prerequisites, sequence constraints, migration needs, and operational-readiness work.

controls.statement: Distinguish committed obligations from targets, options, and exploratory work.
controls.primary_reason: Roadmap work states form a closed classification whose explicit values can be validated.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every roadmap item is labeled committed obligation, target, option, or exploratory work.

controls.statement: Define entry and exit criteria for roadmap stages.
controls.primary_reason: Roadmap stage entry and exit criteria are exact required structured predicates.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every roadmap stage defines versioned entry and exit criteria.

controls.statement: Document who made material priority decisions and why.
controls.primary_reason: Material priority decisions can be required to record decision-maker identity and rationale.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every priority decision marked material contains authenticated decision-maker identity and nonempty rationale.

controls.statement: Define event semantics and data-quality requirements before instrumenting them.
controls.primary_reason: Event contracts, quality rules, and timestamps can be compared with instrumentation introduction dates.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every instrumented event has versioned semantics and data-quality requirements effective before the instrumentation version.

controls.statement: Pre-register experiment hypothesis, population, unit, allocation, duration, primary measure, guardrails, and stopping rules.
controls.primary_reason: The experiment fields and preregistration timestamp are explicit and can be validated before allocation begins.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Before exposure starts, the experiment record fixes hypothesis, population, unit, allocation, duration, primary measure, guardrails, and stopping rules.

controls.statement: Preserve experiment configuration, code, data lineage, analysis, and decision records.
controls.primary_reason: Immutable experiment manifests and lineage references can prove preservation of configuration, code, data, analysis, and decision records.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every experiment preserves versioned configuration, code digest, data-lineage graph, analysis artifact, and decision record.

controls.statement: Define feature-flag cleanup, long-term holdout, and post-launch validation plans.
controls.primary_reason: Cleanup, holdout, and validation plans are three explicit feature-flag lifecycle artifacts.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every experiment feature flag has versioned cleanup, long-term holdout, and post-launch validation plans or explicit inapplicability decisions.

controls.statement: Define lifecycle states and entry, support, maintenance, deprecation, and retirement criteria.
controls.primary_reason: Lifecycle states and the five transition or service criteria groups are explicit versioned schema elements.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The lifecycle policy defines states plus entry, support, maintenance, deprecation, and retirement criteria.

controls.statement: Track adoption, usage, critical customers, integrations, dependencies, and data before deprecation.
controls.primary_reason: The six deprecation input classes are finite inventory and measurement fields with a before-deprecation timestamp requirement.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Before deprecation approval, the record contains adoption, usage, critical-customer, integration, dependency, and data inventories.

controls.statement: Define how defects and vulnerabilities are handled during maintenance and extended-support periods.
controls.primary_reason: Maintenance and extended-support handling rules are explicit policy fields for defects and vulnerabilities.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The lifecycle policy defines intake, severity, response, fix, disclosure, and exception handling for defects and vulnerabilities in each support period.

controls.statement: Prevent new dependencies on components already marked for retirement.
controls.primary_reason: Retirement status and dependency graphs are structured, allowing new dependency edges to retired components to be blocked exactly.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every component marked for retirement has an effective retirement-state timestamp.
No dependency edge created after that timestamp targets the retiring component.

controls.statement: Measure migration progress and contact customers at risk of disruption.
controls.primary_reason: A migration population, progress state, risk rule, and notification log provide fixed coverage and delivery checks.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every migration subject has a current progress state and an evaluated disruption-risk status.
Every subject marked at risk has authenticated contact evidence through the declared channel.

controls.statement: Keep old and new versions interoperable for the documented transition where required.
controls.primary_reason: A documented transition matrix and applicability decisions create finite old-new version pairs with exact interoperability expectations.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every version pair required during the documented transition has a current successful interoperability test result.

controls.statement: Define final data export, retention, deletion, legal hold, and backup behavior.
controls.primary_reason: The six final data-handling behaviors are explicit retirement-plan fields with applicability decisions.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The retirement plan defines final export, retention, deletion, legal-hold, and backup behavior for every applicable data class.

controls.statement: Revoke credentials, domains, certificates, endpoints, jobs, queues, infrastructure, and supplier access during retirement.
controls.primary_reason: A retirement resource inventory and authenticated provider or environment state can prove revocation for each finite item.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The retirement manifest enumerates credentials, domains, certificates, endpoints, jobs, queues, infrastructure, and supplier access.
Every inventoried item is revoked, disabled, or removed in authenticated current environment state.

controls.statement: Verify that retired assets are no longer reachable, billed, monitored as active, or processing data.
controls.primary_reason: A finite retired-asset inventory supports exact reachability, billing, monitor-state, and data-processing queries.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every retired asset is unreachable, absent from active billing, disabled in active-monitor inventories, and produces no data-processing events.
